page.title: Settings
page.allowedHostsHint: Comma-separated host names, besides IP addresses, localhost and *.local.
page.namingHint: Placeholders: {'{'}title{'}'} {'{'}year{'}'} {'{'}season{'}'} {'{'}episode{'}'} {'{'}episodeTitle{'}'} {'{'}channel{'}'} {'{'}date{'}'}; numbers with leading zeros: {'{'}episode:02{'}'}. Parts in [square brackets] are left out when a placeholder in them is empty, e.g. {'{'}title{'}'}[ ({'{'}year{'}'})].
page.folderHint: Empty = recordings stay where they are. Otherwise a path below the recording folder with the same placeholders, e.g. {'{'}title{'}'}/Season {'{'}season:02{'}'} or Films.
page.pushServerHint: ntfy.sh is the public service; if you run your own ntfy server, enter its address.
page.leaveUnsaved: There are unsaved changes. Leave the page anyway?
page.plexUrlHint: Easiest with “Sign in with Plex” below. By hand: the address the box reaches the server at, e.g. http://192.168.1.10:32400 or https://plex.example.org.
page.plexFallbackUrlsHint: Tried in order when the address above doesn't answer — e.g. its home-network address (http://192.168.1.10:32400) next to a domain. Signing in with Plex fills them in; separate several with commas.

tokens.title: API tokens
tokens.subtitle: For app and API clients — separate from the sign-in password above, and revocable on its own.
tokens.createdOnce: Copy this now — it won't be shown again.
tokens.devBody: Call the API with the token as a bearer token. Add box=<id> to say which box a request is about (the box IDs are listed by GET /api/v1/boxes); without it the first box is used. Changes are two steps: a …/plan call returns a preview, POST /api/v1/plans/{'{'}id{'}'}/apply applies it.
tokens.devBodyOne: Call the API with the token as a bearer token. Changes are two steps: a …/plan call returns a preview, POST /api/v1/plans/{'{'}id{'}'}/apply applies it.

install.title: DreamHub as an app
install.standalone: DreamHub is running as an installed app here.
install.prompt: Put DreamHub on your home screen or desktop: it opens in its own window, without the browser's address bar.
install.ios: In Safari, tap Share, then “Add to Home Screen”. DreamHub then opens full screen like an app.
install.needsHttps: Browsers only offer to install an app over HTTPS, and DreamHub is open over plain http here. On an iPhone or iPad, Share → “Add to Home Screen” works anyway. For Android and desktops, the user guide shows how to put DreamHub behind HTTPS.

docker.setUpIntro: Docker runs the apps. DreamHub downloads it once and keeps everything in the box's /data memory.

intro.packages: Software for the box itself (DreamOS): TV plugins, skins and tools.
intro.extensions: Extensions are small add-ons for DreamHub itself — for example one that switches a smart plug. They show up here as a card.
intro.docker: Optional: extra apps in containers — not needed for normal operation.

apps.portHint: The port you open it on. The default is fine unless something else uses it.

apps.searchTitle: Look for other apps on Docker Hub

uninstall.title: Uninstall Docker
uninstall.intro: Stops the apps and removes Docker from the box. Recordings and TV are not affected.
uninstall.question: Also delete the app data?
uninstall.questionHint: Off: the apps' settings and files stay, so the apps can come back after Docker is set up again.

step.containers: Stop and remove all app containers DreamHub created ({count}).

custom.title: Add your own container
custom.intro: Paste a compose file, name an image, or import an Unraid template. You get the same form as for the apps above.
custom.responsibility: You are responsible for what you run. A container can use the box's memory and disk and slow down TV and recordings. DreamHub checks which folders it may see — the system, DreamHub's own data and other apps' data are always refused — but it can't judge the software itself.
custom.responsibilityShort: You are responsible for what this container does on the box.
custom.composeHelp: Supported: services with image, ports, volumes, environment, command, memory limit, restart and depends_on. Everything else is refused with a reason. Variables like {example} become form fields.
custom.imageHelp: For example ghcr.io/someone/tool:1.2 or nginx. Add ports, variables and folders on the next screen under advanced options.
custom.unraidHelp: Paste the template's XML. Nothing is downloaded and DreamHub bundles no templates; only ports, folders and variables are read.
custom.hostNetwork: Runs on the box's own network
custom.hostNetworkHint: Every container shares the box's network (the only kind this box allows), so the app listens on its own ports directly. Containers of one app reach each other on 127.0.0.1.

issue.unsupported_key: “{key}” isn't supported ({where}). DreamHub reads services with image, ports, volumes, environment, command, memory limit, restart and depends_on.

issue.volume_anonymous: A folder without a source ({where}): give it a name or a path so it is kept.
issue.network_mode: The network mode “{detail}” isn't supported ({where}). Apps use the box's own network.
issue.depends_cycle: The services wait for each other in a circle.
issue.service_name: The service name “{detail}” can't be used.
issue.mem_invalid: The memory limit isn't a size like 512m or 1g ({where}).
issue.ext_invalid: DreamHub's own settings in the file (x-dreamhub) can't be used: {detail}
issue.mount_refused: The folder {key} can't be given to a container: {reason}.
issue.device_refused: The device {key} can't be given to a container (raw memory, the kernel log and the box's flash are never allowed).
issue.key_ignored: “{key}” is ignored — DreamHub manages that itself ({where}).
issue.restart_managed: Restarting is managed by DreamHub: a crashing app is restarted a few times and then reported.
issue.service_hostname: {key} refers to the service “{detail}” by name. On this box all containers share one network, so use 127.0.0.1 there.
issue.unraid_icon: The template's icon is not loaded (DreamHub makes no outside requests).
issue.unraid_privileged: The template runs the container privileged — installing it will ask for an extra confirmation.
issue.unraid_network: The network “{detail}” is ignored; apps run on the box's own network.
issue.unraid_extraparams: The template's extra docker parameters are not used: DreamHub never passes free-form docker arguments.
issue.unraid_ignored: Left out: {detail} (devices and labels are not imported).
issue.unraid_port_remap: Unraid maps host ports to container ports. Here apps use the box's own network, so each app listens on its container port itself.
issue.unraid_paths: The template's folders are replaced by folders in the app's storage. Pick real folders below /media in the form if the app needs your files.
issue.unraid_skipped: “{detail}” was left out because it can't be used.

riskWhy.output: A wrong value can leave the TV black or without sound. If the picture is gone, put the value back on the TV.
riskWhy.access: A wrong value can lock DreamHub and other apps out of the box (port, login, network, remote control). It may then only be fixable on the TV.
riskWhy.tuner: A wrong value can stop reception on a tuner until the configuration is put back.
riskWhy.parental: Changes the parental lock or its PIN. A forgotten PIN keeps channels or menus locked.
riskWhy.power: Changes how the receiver goes to standby, switches off or wakes up — a recording or a wake-up for a timer may not happen.
riskWhy.sideeffects: A wrong value can switch the TV or other devices on and off at odd moments.
riskWhy.storage: A path that does not exist, or a disk that is not there, stops recordings and timeshift.
riskWhy.streaming: Affects streaming and transcoding; a wrong value can make streams stop working.
riskWhy.hardware: Affects fans, front panel or picture enhancement at once; the effect is visible or audible immediately.

boxsettings.guiRestartWhy: A change takes effect only after the receiver's user interface is restarted (Restart GUI).
boxsettings.secretWhy: This is a password or PIN. DreamHub never shows it — only whether it is set.

help.recording_margin_before: How many minutes before the programme's start the recording begins, so the first seconds are not lost. A longer margin uses more disk space and can overlap with the recording before.
help.recording_margin_after: How many minutes the recording runs on after the programme's planned end — useful for programmes that overrun.
help.recording_adjust_time_to_event: Moves a timer's start and end to the times the programme guide gives, when those differ from what the timer says.
help.usage_hdd_standby: How long the disk may stay idle before it spins down. A short time saves power and noise; opening a recording after a spin-down takes a few seconds longer.
help.usage_setup_level: Decides how many settings the receiver's own menus — and this page — list: simple, advanced or expert. DreamHub shows what the box lists for its own level; to see more, raise the level on the TV.
help.hdmicec_enabled: Lets the receiver and the TV control each other over the HDMI cable: switching on and off together, remote control, volume. The other settings in this section decide what is sent. A wrong setting can switch the TV on or off at odd moments.
help.hdmicec_disabletimerwakeup: Does not switch the TV on when the receiver wakes up for a timer — the recording starts without the TV lighting up.
help.hdmicec_avvolumecontrol: Uses the A/V receiver connected over HDMI for the volume instead of the receiver's own output.
help.hdmicec_enabletvrc: Lets the TV's remote control operate this receiver.
help.hdmicec_message_delay: The pause between two messages to the TV. A longer pause helps with TVs that miss quick messages.
help.av_generalAC3delay: Delays the Dolby Digital sound against the picture, in milliseconds. Use it when the sound is out of step with the picture on a receiver or soundbar.
help.av_generalPCMdelay: Delays the PCM (stereo) sound against the picture, in milliseconds. Use it when the sound is out of step with the picture.
help.av_bypass_edid_checking: Ignores what the TV says it can show and sends the picture anyway. Meant for finding the cause of a black screen; the picture may then be in a mode the TV cannot show.
help.av_downmix_ac3: Mixes Dolby Digital and DTS sound down to stereo on the outputs that carry only two channels.
help.av_avl: Automatic volume levelling: keeps loud adverts and quiet scenes at a more even volume.
help.autoshutdown_autostart: Switches the receiver completely off after it has been in standby for the time set below.
help.autoshutdown_time: How many minutes the receiver stays in standby before it switches itself off.
help.autoshutdown_enableinactivity: Lets the receiver act after a time with no key presses and no recording — go to standby or switch off, as set below.
help.autoshutdown_inactivetime: How many minutes without key presses before the action below happens.
help.autoshutdown_inactivityaction: What the receiver does after that time without key presses.
help.autoshutdown_epgrefresh: Keeps the receiver from switching off while it is updating the programme guide.
help.usage_ts_auto_start: Starts timeshift by itself after the time chosen on a channel. Timeshift is a rolling recording of the live programme that lets you pause and rewind it.
help.usage_ts_min_duration: Timeshift recordings shorter than this many minutes are not kept.
help.usage_ts_clean_ts_older_than: Deletes timeshift files that are older than this many days.

boxsettings.needsPlugin: This Dreambox needs a newer DreamHub plugin to show its settings. Update the DreamHub package on the box.
boxsettings.treeWhy: A setting from the box's configuration, listed by its key name — it has no menu text. Plugins mostly read these when they start, so a change may need a restart of the plugin or the GUI.
boxsettings.stateWhy: This looks like something the box keeps for itself (the last channel, a counter, a time), not a choice you made.
boxsettings.levelAll: Setup mode of the box: {level}. Every setting is listed here, whatever its level; the level of each shows beside it.
